title: Rahab's scarlet cord (Joshua 2)
hookLine: a woman on the city wall hides two spies and hangs a red cord from her window

lines: TWO SPIES, ONE HOUSE IN THE WALL.
A RED LINE IN THE WINDOW.
cards: A red line hangs from a window in a city wall. Joshua has sent two men across the river to spy out Jericho, and in the King James words they "came into an harlot's house, named Rahab, and lodged there."
Her house is built into the town wall. The king hears that spies are inside, and his men come to her door. Rahab has already hidden the spies on her roof, under stalks of flax.
She tells them the strangers left at dark: hurry, and you'll catch them.

teach.b: Rahab gives her reason, and it's an outsider's confession. Her city has heard what Israel's God has done, and their hearts have melted.
Then, in the King James Bible: "for the LORD your God, he is God in heaven above, and in earth beneath." Those words echo, almost exactly, what Moses tells Israel in Deuteronomy.
A Canaanite woman, in a city about to fall, speaks Israel's own creed back to Israel's spies. Then she asks for one thing. The Hebrew word is chesed: loyal kindness.
I showed you kindness; show kindness to my father's house. Spare my parents, my brothers, my sisters. The spies agree.
She lets them down from her window by a cord, and they tell her: "thou shalt bind this line of scarlet thread in the window which thou didst let us down by." Everyone inside will be safe.
Then, as soon as they're gone: "And she bound the scarlet line in the window."

teach.h: SHE TIES IT BEFORE THE ARMY COMES.
teach.b: She doesn't wait for the army. She hangs the sign of the promise while nothing has happened yet, and lives under it.

Some Christian readers see the thread as a picture of rescue through blood, like the blood on the doorposts at Passover. Others see a woman staking her family on a promise from strangers. The story doesn't end at Jericho.

teach.h: HEBREWS, JAMES AND MATTHEW NAME HER.
teach.b: Hebrews names her: "By faith the harlot Rahab perished not with them that believed not, when she had received the spies with peace." James praises what she did.
Matthew's family line of Jesus includes a Rachab, traditionally taken to be her. The woman on the wall ends up inside the story.

how: Christians meet Rahab in sermons on Hebrews 11 and on welcoming outsiders, and some churches teach the scarlet cord as a sign of rescue.

a promise sealed with an oath

s: Rahab ties the scarlet line only when the army arrives
she binds it as soon as the spies are gone: "and she bound the scarlet line in the window."
Rahab's words about God echo Moses in Deuteronomy
he is God in heaven above, and in earth beneath.
the New Testament never mentions Rahab
Hebrews and James name her, and Matthew's family line of Jesus includes a Rachab, traditionally taken to be her.

games.q: you're Rahab. the king's men are at your door asking for two Israelite spies, who are hidden on your roof. what do you do?
o: hide them and send the king's men away.
run with them to the Israelite camp.
games.why: she tells the searchers to hurry after men already gone, then asks the spies for kindness to her family. readers still argue about her lie; Hebrews remembers her for her faith.

practice: Rahab's risk was her life; yours can be smaller: speaking up for someone being talked about, sitting with the person nobody sits with, siding out loud with the unpopular one.
Let one person come to mind who could use someone on their side, and ask what it would cost you to help. If you pray, hold them up by name; if not, keep them in mind and breathe.

wordCard.voice: Chesed. Hebrew for loyal kindness: what Rahab asked the spies to answer, the kindness she had shown them, with kindness for her family.

orig.note: Hebrew: loyal kindness. Rahab asks the spies to answer her chesed with chesed (Joshua 2:12).

carryVoice: Your line: the cord in the window. She tied it before anything had happened. See you tomorrow.
